questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Travelling to an english speaking country, making it possible to study and connect with people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing exchange. Can only recommend others doing it. It will completely change your vision!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. We had a lot of pre-arrival courses guiding the students in the right direction.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance on the important locations on campus area, to receive our stuff.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Typical student housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my student facillity, we were 4 students sharing common kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Really good options. You get to live with other students and spend time together.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration of courses was ok at UBC

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could search for help at UBC website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not too successful. Had to apply for 10 courses to get 3.  Got 4th, 6th, and 8th priority. So in the beginning not really the courses i had hoped. But got to enjoy all at the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just doing a lot of research, and make sure you are permitted to take your desired courses. It turned out i wasn't allowed my 2nd and 3rd priority.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3rd year courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had 3 courses in total. The first two were the same kind of teaching as in KU. The 3rd course was only online lessons.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all my listed courses. They are all different in their own way, but give you a lot of insight.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: The clubs at UBC were amazing!

questions.answer: Swimming, surfing, running, skiing, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All sorts of sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking the surrounding nature of Vancouver. Do it in september and october before it gets too cold.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy, the reason being that the main language is english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Make sure all arriving exchange create a common group chat, for example on WhatsApp.
Also join local clubs on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Did not really experience any cultural difficulties.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Vancouver, Canada has a really diverce culture, making it so exciting to meet new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to get engaged with the other exchange students as soon as possible. You will be doing the local activities and hikes together.
Explore as much of the surrounding area as possible.
Enjoy your unforgettable stay!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do the hikings as soon as possible in september and october. Vancouver area gets really rainy in november and december.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My personal development. The exchange semester has complelety reshaped how i view the world and other people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to do as much as possible doing my 4 month exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
